summary:
Davao Region has no regional statute or regional ordinance of its own governing sexual orientation or gender identity. A trans visitor to the region stands under the national framework of the Philippines, together with the municipal law of the particular city or municipality visited.

Davao City, the region's administrative center, is recorded among the Philippine localities that have a non-discrimination ordinance. Its council passed the measure in December 2012, banning discrimination against gays (LGBT people), minorities and differently-abled persons. Within Davao City, that ordinance is the only documented local layer of protection available beyond the national position.

Custody practice specific to the region is documented. The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology in Davao moves LGBT detainees in batches to the City Jail Annex, holding them alongside persons with disabilities, the sick and senior citizens as a stated measure to prevent abuse. Placement of trans detainees in Davao thus takes the form of administrative segregation rather than gender-matched accommodation.
tangentialFactors:
Protection in Davao Region is municipal rather than regional, so a trans traveller's position changes with the city or municipality visited: inside Davao City the 2012 ordinance applies, while elsewhere in the region the visitor falls back on the national position alone. The inventory documents no comparable ordinance in any other Davao Region municipality.

The Davao City measure addresses gays (LGBT people), minorities and differently-abled persons within a single instrument, so its protected grounds are framed in sexual-orientation and disability terms as much as in gender-identity terms.
localsOnly:
For residents, the practical protection available in the region is the Davao City ordinance of December 2012, which covers discrimination against gays (LGBT people), minorities and differently-abled persons within the city's jurisdiction. No equivalent regional instrument extends that coverage to the rest of Davao Region.

A resident taken into custody in Davao is held under the batch-transfer arrangement to the City Jail Annex, where LGBT detainees are placed with persons with disabilities, the sick and senior citizens.
outOfScopeNotes:
The substantive reach of the Davao City ordinance is not established by the sources: whether it covers employment, accommodation, service provision, education or health care is not stated, and no penalties under the ordinance are recorded.

Whether the ordinance treats gender identity as a protected ground distinct from sexual orientation is unresolved; the sources describe its coverage as gays (LGBT people), minorities and differently-abled persons.

The enforcement record of the ordinance is not sourced, and no refusal of service, prosecution or trans-specific violence in Davao Region appears in the inventory. No regional incident figures are available, so no regional violence rate can be stated or compared against a general homicide rate.
